title: Syndication desk and archive review
not_questions: We will not license Adobe Workfront.
Submit time estimates in desk shifts of eight hours.

questions.text: Describe how AEM Assets would record a clip's territory rights and expiry date before the syndication desk can distribute it.
Explain how AEM Assets would flag a music license that expires ahead of the wider programme rights.
Provide an AEM Assets acceptance test for ingesting two archive transfers from Amazon S3 that carry the same tape identifier.
Show how AEM Assets would trace a withdrawn still image to its replacement without changing the approved programme title.
Describe how Frame.io would separate the comments on a captioned cut from those on the clean international version.
Explain how Frame.io would give a freelance subtitle reviewer access to one programme for a fixed review window.
Provide a Frame.io review exercise in which the producer returns a cut to the editor after a legal clearance fails.
Show how Frame.io would preserve the approved cut reference when the editor submits a later version for domestic use.
Identify the supplier's proposed archive migration lead and state their availability during our festival blackout.
Provide two client references from teams that distribute licensed programmes across more than one territory.
Describe your firm's support coverage when a rights dispute arises during a weekend broadcast.
Quote your company's day rate for an extra training session for freelance producers.
